page: Amazon Web Services d3en.2xlarge is a dense storage instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz and includes a 35 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, translating to 4.0 GB of RAM per core.

A defining characteristic of this instance is its massive local storage capacity, offering 55,920 GB of HDD storage. This makes the instance highly optimized for dense storage workloads. For network connectivity, the d3en.2xlarge provides a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps, supporting efficient data transfer rates for large-scale storage operations.

Benchmark results indicate average multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 6980.42 and a Passmark CPU score of 7724.51. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 1326.69 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1161.0. Memory bandwidth is moderate, reaching 400.69 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 51.86 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The instance exhibits weak performance in Redis SET operations and poor performance in medium-sized LLM inference tasks.

Given the massive local HDD storage coupled with moderate compute capabilities, the d3en.2xlarge offers high qualitative cost efficiency for storage-dense applications where high-capacity local storage is prioritized over raw compute power. It is well-suited for workloads such as large-scale data warehousing, distributed file systems, data lakes, and massive database storage.
